context.text: In a survey of 721 Delhi street vendors in 2024, 80% saw fewer customers during heatwaves and 49% lost income.

source.label: Greenpeace India and National Hawkers Federation, 2024

context.text: Doctors at two Indian hospitals said more than 90% of their heat-illness patients in 2024 were outdoor workers.
Rickshaw pullers in Dhaka have described their earnings falling from about Tk 1,200 to Tk 700–800 a day in extreme heat, with fewer passengers and shorter hours.
In a 2024 heatwave, one puller returned his rickshaw after a few hours and still owed the day’s Tk 150 rent.

In April 2024 the Bangladesh Red Crescent acted on the heat forecast in Dhaka: cash grants of at least Tk 5,000 to 4,000 households, three cooling stations with more than 15,000 visits, and caps for 3,500 rickshaw and van pullers.
Dhaka North appointed a chief heat officer in 2023, and the city has given rickshaw pullers umbrellas, water and saline, and planned shaded cooling zones.

A national survey found 176,373 manual workers, including family members, in Nepal’s brick kilns, which operate seasonally from October to June. Over three-quarters (75.7%) received a pay advance from a labour contractor.

source.label: Central Bureau of Statistics, ILO and UNICEF, 2020

context.text: In late May 2026, temperatures in Dhangadhi and Nepalgunj in the western Terai reached around 38 °C before noon, and heatstroke patients were arriving at Bheri Hospital every day.
Nepal recorded 89 days above the historical 90th-percentile temperature between May 2024 and May 2025.
Under the national health insurance programme, a family of up to five pays Rs 3,500 a year for treatment worth up to Rs 100,000.
Researchers in Nepal have proposed heat stress limits for different workloads, drawing on measurements in sectors including brick kilns.

source.label: Heat Standard Across Different Workloads in Nepal, 2024

countries.name: Sri Lanka
countries.tempNote: Air temperatures. With coastal humidity, the heat index in the Western Province has reached the Department of Meteorology’s ‘caution’ level.

context.text: In March 2024 the Department of Meteorology issued heat advisories for the Western Province and others, urging people to stay hydrated and work in the shade.

In 2023, when fish traders at Peliyagoda raised concerns about the price of ice, the Ministry of Fisheries brought traders and ice suppliers together and agreed a lower price: Rs 650 for 50 kg instead of Rs 850.
A national strategy on fish loss names the high cost of energy for fishing, ice and transport as a weakness, and aims to cut quality loss in the multi-day fishery by 30% by 2033.

source.label: FAO: food loss and waste in fish value chains, Sri Lanka

context.text: Sri Lanka has provided free public health care to its whole population since 1951.
The 2026 minimum wage for garment, footwear and travel goods workers is US$210 a month, plus a US$7 transport or housing allowance and a US$10 monthly attendance bonus.
In April 2024 the Ministry of Labour asked factories to spray water on roofs, install enough fans, open windows, provide more clean drinking water and assign staff to watch workplace thermometers.
At three garment factories in Phnom Penh, workers reporting heat symptoms rose from 68% in the cooler months to 88% in the hot months, by their own reports.

source.label: Chea et al., BMC Public Health, 2025

context.text: The National Social Security Fund’s health care scheme covers private-sector workers at contracted public and private facilities.

countries.name: Indonesia
countries.tempNote: Air temperatures. Jakarta’s humidity makes the heat feel hotter than the reading.

context.text: A 2023 survey of 225 app-based motorbike riders around Jakarta found an average daily income of Rp171,600.
Riders pay their own running costs; a transport ministry survey put them at Rp50,000–100,000 a day.
In hot spells, Jakarta’s health office has advised drinking more water, covering up and limiting strenuous outdoor activity between 11 am and 3 pm.
The government has halved work-accident and death insurance contributions for app-based riders and other transport workers, to Rp8,400 a month, from January 2026 to March 2027.

countries.name: Philippines
countries.tempNote: Air temperatures. The heat index, which adds humidity, reached 46 °C at Manila’s airport on 24 April 2024.

context.text: On 5 April 2024, 5,288 schools switched from in-person classes to remote learning because of the heat, affecting more than 3.6 million students.
School heads can suspend in-person classes when the heat index is high, under a 2022 Department of Education order.
PAGASA recorded a heat index of 46 °C at NAIA in Pasay City on 24 April 2024, the highest in Metro Manila that year.

The Department of Labor and Employment has reminded employers to adjust rest breaks, provide free drinking water and ventilate workplaces in the hot season. Self-employed vendors work outside these workplace measures.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.tempNote: Air temperatures. With Singapore’s humidity, the heat stress index can reach the level at which longer rest breaks are required.

context.text: Singapore’s heat stress framework for outdoor work requires rest under shade, regular drinking water and at least a week of acclimatisation, with hourly rest breaks of at least 15 minutes for heavy work in the highest heat stress. More measures become legal requirements from 1 December 2026.

source.label: Ministry of Manpower: heat stress measures for outdoor work

context.text: The Ministry of Manpower has taken enforcement action against workplaces found not meeting the heat measures, including for inadequate shaded rest breaks.
Employers must pay for medical treatment of their Work Permit holders and hold at least S$60,000 of medical insurance a year for each.
Standards for new dormitories, announced in 2021, cap rooms at 12 residents and require enough fans for air circulation; existing dormitories are to be upgraded over time.

In a 2025 survey of more than 1,000 informal workers in Bangkok, nearly 80% cut their working hours because of heat, and three-quarters of home-based workers lost at least one working day a month to heat-related illness, their own or a family member’s.
Thailand’s health ministry counted 61 heatstroke deaths between January and early May 2024, more than in the whole of 2023.
In April 2024 Bangkok warned that the heat index could rise above 52 °C, the ‘extremely dangerous’ level.

Since October 2025, informal workers in the voluntary social security scheme (Section 40) receive 200 baht for an outpatient visit when a doctor orders at least a day of rest, for up to three visits a year.
In early 2024 a long heatwave and drought brought salt water far inland in the Mekong Delta; about 73,900 households had limited access to fresh water.
In an earlier salinity crisis in Ben Tre, households bought fresh water for daily use at about ₫150,000–200,000 a cubic metre.
A national study estimated nearly US$3 billion a year in crop losses from saltwater intrusion.
Health insurance covers about 93% of Vietnam’s population, and the state pays for cards for poor households.

people.name: Rekha
people.where: A cart on a market road
people.intro: Rekha buys vegetables at dawn and sells from a cart until dark. What does not sell by evening, she loses.
people.heatLine: Customers stay indoors; {pr} packs up {h} hours early and some stock goes soft.

people.name: Sunil
people.where: A labour naka, waiting to be hired
people.intro: Sunil waits at the naka from 7 a.m. If a contractor picks him, he works the day. If he is not there, someone else is picked.
people.costLabel: Bus fare to the naka and site
people.heatLine: Work is cut by {h} hours in the afternoon heat, and {pr} is paid only for the hours worked.

people.name: Farida
people.where: A one-room home under a tin roof
people.intro: Farida stitches garments at home, paid by the piece. The tin roof turns the room into an oven by noon, and it stays hot at night.
people.heatLine: The room is too hot to work for {h} hours; {pr} finishes fewer pieces after a sleepless night.

people.name: Rahim
people.where: The streets of Dhaka, on a rented rickshaw
people.intro: Rahim rents a rickshaw from a garage owner every morning. Whatever he earns, the day’s rent is owed when he returns it.
people.costLabel: Rickshaw rent to the garage owner
people.heatLine: Few passengers in the midday heat; {pr} rests for {h} hours, but the full day’s rent is still owed.
people.heatLineFree: Few passengers in the midday heat; {pr} rests for {h} hours, and the day’s rent is waived on the alert.

people.name: Sreymom
people.where: A garment factory outside Phnom Penh
people.intro: Sreymom sews on a factory line under a metal roof. Her monthly wage is protected; the overtime that pays for her family’s extras is not, and missing a day loses the month’s attendance bonus.
people.homeLabel: Food, rent and money sent home
people.heatLine: The line slows in the afternoon heat; {h} hours of overtime are cut.

people.name: Kumar
people.where: A building site, and a dormitory at night
people.intro: Kumar works on a building site and sleeps in a dormitory room. His basic pay is monthly; overtime is what he sends home. The law already gives him rest breaks and medical care.
people.homeLabel: Food, phone and money sent home
people.heatLine: Work pauses in the worst heat; {h} hours of overtime are lost.

rest.name: Rest breaks under the heat framework
rest.does: Shaded rest breaks every hour in the highest heat stress, as Singapore’s framework requires; his pay continues.

conds.text: Heat stress is measured at his worksite, not only by the nearest weather station
Supervisors schedule the breaks, and they are checked

people.name: Kamala
people.where: A brick kiln in the Terai, for the dry season
people.intro: Kamala moulds bricks in the open from first light, paid by the thousand. She took a pay advance from the labour contractor before the season; part of each day’s pay goes against it.
people.heatLine: Moulding stops in the midday heat; {pr} loses {h} hours of bricks, and the advance is still repaid.
people.heatLineFree: Moulding stops in the midday heat; {pr} loses {h} hours of bricks, but repayment pauses on the alert.

people.name: Budi
people.where: Jakarta’s roads, on his own motorbike
people.intro: Budi carries passengers and food orders through an app. He pays for his own fuel, phone data and motorbike, and the day’s incentive depends on how many trips he completes.
people.heatLine: Fewer orders and slower trips in the midday heat; {pr} loses {h} hours of work.

rest.name: A heat pause that keeps the incentive
rest.does: Logging off in the hottest hours, on official heat advice, does not count against his trip target or rating.

conds.text: The platform agrees to it, with riders’ associations
It is tied to official heat advice, so everyone knows when it applies

people.name: Lan
people.where: A small rice farm in the Mekong Delta
people.intro: Lan farms her family’s rice field and works on neighbours’ farms for a daily wage. In the dry season, salt water creeps up the canals; drinking water has to be stored or bought.
people.costLabel: Fuel for the pump and tools
people.heatLine: Field work stops in the midday heat; {pr} loses {h} hours of wages.

people.name: Nimal
people.where: Negombo, buying at the landing site and selling by bicycle
people.intro: Nimal buys fish at the landing site at dawn and sells it from an iced box on his bicycle. In the heat, fish spoils faster: he needs more ice, and what does not sell by midday loses its value.
people.heatLine: Fish spoils faster in the heat; {pr} buys extra ice and stops selling {h} hours early.

freecare.name: Free care at a public clinic
freecare.does: Treatment at a government clinic or hospital, free at the point of use.

conds.text: A public clinic or hospital is open within reach
He is seen without losing the whole day waiting

shade.name: Shade and water at the market
shade.does: Shade over the selling spots, and a refill point.

people.name: Joy
people.where: A cart on a busy street in Metro Manila
people.intro: Joy sells snacks and cold drinks from a cart. When heat suspends in-person classes, her children are at home, and looking after them falls to her.
people.heatLine: Few buyers in the midday heat, and the children are home with classes suspended; {pr} loses {h} hours of selling.

people.name: Malee
people.where: Her rented room in Bangkok, under a metal roof
people.intro: Malee sews garments at home, paid by the piece. Her room is also where she cooks and sleeps; in the afternoon heat, the work slows and the fan runs all day.
people.heatLine: The room is too hot to sew in the afternoon; {pr} loses {h} hours of pieces.

measures.name: Shade and water where they work
measures.does: Shade and a refill point at the spot where they work or wait.
measures.assume: Assumed: recovers 1 working hour on hot days, and no water to buy.

conds.text: It is at the spot where {pr} actually works or waits
Someone refills and repairs it every day

measures.name: Paid rest breaks on site
measures.does: Breaks in the hottest hours that are paid, so stopping does not mean losing pay.
measures.assume: Protects pay for up to 2 lost hours on hot days.

conds.text: The contractor agrees, in writing
Someone checks that breaks are really given

measures.name: A cooling station
measures.does: A shaded or cooled rest point with water, salts and first aid.
measures.assume: Assumed: recovers 1 working hour on hot days.

conds.text: It is where {pr} works or waits, not across town
It is open during working hours
{Pr} can step in without losing the day’s work
Water and a caretaker are paid for

measures.name: A cool roof
measures.does: A reflective coating on the tin roof over the room where she works and sleeps.
measures.assume: Assumed: recovers 1 working hour on hot days. One-off cost, not paid by her.

conds.text: The landlord agrees, and the rent does not rise
Someone pays to recoat it in a few years

measures.name: An efficient fan and lifeline power
measures.does: A fan, and an electricity tariff she can afford in the hottest weeks.
measures.assume: Assumed: recovers 1 working hour on hot days; costs {power} a day in power unless the tariff is protected.

conds.text: Power stays on in the afternoon peak
A lifeline tariff covers the extra units

measures.name: Cash before the heat
measures.does: A payment released on the heat forecast, before the worst days.
measures.assume: You set the amount and the day it arrives.

conds.text: {Pr} is registered, with an ID and a way to receive money
Someone {pr} trusts told {obj} about it

measures.name: Heat income insurance
measures.does: Pays a fixed amount when an official heat reading crosses a threshold.
measures.assume: You set the payout. Reported payments have taken six to eight weeks.

conds.text: {Pr} is enrolled and the premium is paid
Someone {pr} trusts explained how it pays
The trigger is measured near where {pr} works

measures.name: Hospital cash
measures.does: Pays a daily amount if admitted to hospital, often only after a minimum stay.
measures.assume: Pays {hosp} a day, only if admitted for 48 hours or more.

conds.text: {Pr} is enrolled

measures.name: Free care for heat illness
measures.does: No fee for seeing a doctor or for medicines for heat illness.
measures.assume: Removes the doctor’s fee and medicines ({doctor} in this example).

conds.text: A clinic is open when {pr} can get there

measures.name: Rent relief on alert days
measures.does: Garage owners waive the day’s rickshaw rent when an official heat alert is issued.
measures.assume: Removes the rent on hot days.

conds.text: Garage owners agree, in an arrangement brokered with the city or a workers’ association
It is tied to an official alert, so everyone knows when it applies

measures.name: A cooler factory floor
measures.does: Roof spraying, fans, open windows, drinking water and a thermometer that someone watches, as the Ministry of Labour has asked.
measures.assume: Assumed: recovers 1 working hour on hot days.

conds.text: The factory carries out the guidance every hot day
A named person watches the thermometer and acts on it

measures.name: Sick days that keep the attendance bonus
measures.does: A day off for heat illness, with a doctor’s note, still counts as present for the monthly bonus.
measures.assume: Protects the month’s attendance bonus if she falls ill.

conds.text: The factory agrees, in writing, with the workers’ representatives

measures.name: Care through the national social security fund
measures.does: Treatment at a clinic contracted by the National Social Security Fund.
measures.assume: Covers the clinic visit ({doctor} in this example).

conds.text: Her employer has registered her with the fund
A contracted clinic is open when she can get there

measures.name: Employer-paid medical care
measures.does: Singapore’s law makes employers pay for their Work Permit holders’ medical treatment.
measures.assume: Removes the clinic fee ({doctor} in this example).

conds.text: The employer pays promptly, as the law requires
He can get to a clinic without losing the day’s work

measures.name: A cooler dormitory room
measures.does: Fans, ventilation and shade on the windows, so the body recovers at night.
measures.assume: Assumed: recovers 1 working hour the next day, after a better night’s sleep.

conds.text: Fans and ventilation work in every room
A hot room can be reported and fixed quickly

measures.name: Work in the cool hours
measures.does: Work starts at first light and stops in the hottest hours, without cutting the day’s pay or piece rate.
measures.assume: Assumed: recovers 1 working hour on hot days.

conds.text: Whoever sets the hours agrees, and pay per piece or per day is unchanged
The heat forecast reaches {obj} the day before

measures.assume: Removes the day’s repayment on hot days.

conds.text: The kiln owner and the contractor agree, in writing
It is tied to an official alert, so everyone knows when it applies

measures.name: Care through national health insurance
measures.does: Treatment for heat illness covered by the family’s health insurance.
measures.assume: Covers the clinic visit ({doctor} in this example).

conds.text: The family is enrolled and the premium is paid
She can use it near the kiln, not only at the health post where she enrolled

measures.name: Rider rest points with water
measures.does: Shaded places to wait between orders, with drinking water, where riders gather.
measures.assume: Assumed: recovers 1 working hour on hot days, and no water to buy.

conds.text: They are where riders actually wait for orders
They are open, and the water is refilled, in the hottest hours

measures.name: Care through national health insurance
measures.does: Treatment at his registered clinic through the national health insurance scheme.
measures.assume: Covers the clinic visit ({doctor} in this example).

conds.text: His membership is active and contributions are up to date
His registered clinic is open when he can get there

measures.name: Stored fresh water for the dry season
measures.does: Household tanks and community storage filled before the salt water arrives.
measures.assume: No drinking water to buy on hot days.

conds.text: The tanks are filled before salinity rises
There is a plan to refill them if the dry season runs long

measures.name: A health insurance card that works locally
measures.does: Treatment for heat illness at the commune health station, covered by health insurance.
measures.assume: Covers the clinic visit ({doctor} in this example).

conds.text: Her card is current
The commune health station has staff and medicines on hot days

measures.name: An insulated box and a fair-price ice point
measures.does: A well-insulated fish box, and ice sold at an agreed price near the landing site.
measures.assume: Assumed: no extra ice to buy on hot days, and less fish spoils.

conds.text: An ice point is near the landing site, at an agreed price
The box is paid for once, not from the day’s takings

measures.name: A cool place for children when classes stop
measures.does: A day-care or community space, cool and supervised, open when heat suspends in-person classes.
measures.assume: Assumed: recovers 1 working hour on hot days.

conds.text: It opens on the same days that classes are suspended
Parents hear about it the evening before

measures.name: Voluntary social security
measures.does: The voluntary scheme for informal workers pays towards a day of doctor-ordered rest.
measures.assume: Pays {sick} when a doctor orders at least a day of rest.

conds.text: She is a member, and her monthly contributions are paid up
She sees a doctor who certifies the rest

measures.name: Universal coverage, near where she lives
measures.does: Treatment for heat illness under the universal coverage scheme.
measures.assume: Removes the clinic costs ({doctor} in this example).

conds.text: She is registered with a unit in Bangkok, not only in her home province
The clinic is open when she can get there

measures.name: A trusted messenger

measures.assume: Makes sure {pr} knows about the cash and the insurance.

conds.text: The messenger’s time is paid for

tests.text: Every payment lands after the week is over.

tests.text: The official reading stays just below the threshold, though it is hotter where they work.

tests.text: The documents or bank account the scheme needs are missing.

Of 721 Delhi street vendors surveyed in 2024, 80% saw fewer customers during heatwaves and 49% lost income.

Doctors at two Indian hospitals said more than 90% of their heat-illness patients in 2024 were outdoor workers.

note: Every worker here is a composite, not a real person. The numbers are examples in local currency a day; change them to match the people you work with. The tool adds up cash. It does not predict illness, productivity or payouts.
workshop: Split into groups, one worker each; mix countries to compare. Give each group 25 minutes.
Set the week to match people you know. Agree the hot days.
Build a package. A measure counts only when every condition holds.
Run every test. Note what breaks, and who would have to fix it.
Fill in who pays and who keeps it running. Mark what is only assumed.
Compare packages across groups: who carries the cost, and what is still unresolved?
